Daily Monitor report of 20 August 2020 (also carried on ReliefWeb). Interpreted as 100 sCh cases and 11 deaths in Kotido District, Karamoja. The article states the outbreak 'broke out two weeks ago', so TL is set to 2020-08-06 and TR to the publication date 2020-08-20. CAVEATS, all of which reduce confidence to 0.5 within the Level 3 news band: (i) 'at least 100 others are admitted' is a floor on admissions at a single health facility, not a line-list case total, so 100 is a lower bound and the true case count is probably higher; (ii) the implied CFR of 11 percent is high but epidemiologically plausible in this setting - the article states 'Kotido District has no hospital, what we have is a health centre with only two medical doctors' and the facility 'lacked specialised beds and fluids', and deaths in Karamoja pastoralist communities frequently occur before presentation; (iii) SINGLE-SOURCE: no corroboration was found in the Uganda MoH weekly epidemiological bulletins for weeks 31-38 of 2020 (all downloaded and searched - Kotido appears in those issues only in maternal-death tables), nor in WHO AFRO bulletins, so this event is documented only by national media. Affected sub-counties per the article: Panyangara, Rengen, Nakapelimoru and Romrom. DOUBLE-COUNTING: Provincial subset - do not sum with national row. The 2020 national rows (AI index 5 = 1361 cases; JHU WHO-annual = 1521 cases) already include this event, and adding Moroto (458, index 4) + Nabilatuk (471, index 76) + Napak (11, index 77) + Busia (6, index 78) + Kotido (100) gives 1046, consistent with a national total of 1361-1521 that also contains unattributed cases.
